category_specific_evidence: Special value involved is df = -inf passed to scipy.special.stdtr and stdtrit in scipy/special/_cdflib_wrappers.pxd.
Original check was `if isinf(df):`, which caught both +inf and -inf and returned ndtr(t) for stdtr or ndtri(p) for stdtrit for -inf.

Fix changes the check to `if isinf(df) and df > 0:` so only +inf takes the normal-distribution shortcut; -inf falls through to the NaN handling (`if isnan(df) or isnan(t):` in stdtr, `if isnan(p) or isnan(df):` in stdtrit).
Correct handling: stdtr and stdtrit with df = -inf must return nan rather than a value from the normal distribution, per the commit message and PR#19933.
Regression test test_stdtr_stdtrit_neg_inf asserts np.all(np.isnan(sp.stdtr(-np.inf, [-np.inf, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, np.inf]))) and np.all(np.isnan(sp.stdtrit(-np.inf, [0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0]))).
Input/output example: stdtr(df=-inf, t) with finite t, buggy output ndtr(t), expected nan; value_kind recorded as float.

The wrapper signatures are declared with double arguments (cdef inline double stdtr(double df, double t); cdef inline double stdtrit(double df, double p)), but no passage states that the defect appears for one dtype and not another, so dtype is left null.
PR discussion says the bug was carried over from the original wrapper for the Fortran implementation; the ncfdtrinc 10^4 search bound in issue#19953 is a separate matter and not part of this fix.
No tolerance is stated for the -inf regression test; rtol=2e-12, atol=0.0 belongs to the unrelated test_nctdtrinc_gh19896.
reproduction_risks: Only df = -inf is the special value in scope; the fix does not change NaN handling in p or t beyond the existing isnan check that follows.
